lines: That day's mission involved a battle in the forest, and under the captain's command we somehow repelled the enemy, but the situation was still far from safe.
For now it looks okay, but there’ll probably be another attack. Let’s get ready while we can.
While everyone hurried about following the captain’s orders, Mai moved terribly clumsy.
She was aware of it, but she thought she could somehow hide it.
I won’t be a burden to anyone. Let’s hurry and set up defenses—
As she tried to step forward, careless as she was, Mai bumped into someone.
She was a classmate who lost her father young and now serves as the head of the Fuuma clan despite her youth.
Being given command of the guerrilla unit, she might be the most promising of their peers.
Bumping into her, being stared at, Mai’s cheeks flushed, but she lowered her face quickly so her expression wouldn’t be read.
I’m fine, so let’s get ready right away—
Wait— I thought something was off; could you be injured?
By shouting so aggressively, she practically announced herself.
…just a little. This… what the— huh!?
Fuuma’s foot barely brushed her, and pain and heat shot up her shin.
—Defense is cancelled! We’ll retreat, gather the valuable supplies, and leave the rest. Move fast!
Ignoring Mai’s protest, his strong arms lifted her body effortlessly.
First we’ll carry the wounded. Just hold on for now.
N‑no, no… because of me the mission will fail— ahh!?
Not seeming to hear Mai at all, Fuuma sprinted through the forest.
I slipped completely into his arms, my heart pounding wildly, but I quickly remembered the situation and pounded his chest.
Please, wait, really... I understand the retreat, I get it! But I'll run on my own...
You can't do that injured. Besides— I can't easily trust the words of someone who can't admit they're unwell.
My shy nature backfired, and ashamed of that blunder, Mai lowered her head dejectedly.
Fuuma's arms squeezed Mai's body even tighter.
It's fine, Fuuma. More importantly— sorry, I went too far. I was only joking, after all.
Fuuma replied awkwardly, seeming to choose his words carefully.
Anyway, there's no need to force yourself to run. I can run if I have to... If the pursuers come, Mai, you handle it.
Instead of the unable-to-run Mai, Fuuma ran, taking over the fight that I, known only for my command ability, would have to face with sheer luck.
The important task of protecting the captain made my chest heat up.
...You don't have to push yourself. First priority is escape; if we're cornered, we'll deal with it.
Perhaps feeling a surge of determination, Fuuma took the lead in giving orders.
While we were discussing, a presence approached from the forest behind us.
I know... First, we run! Mai, hold me tighter, I need a stable stance to run!
Being told to cling to a male classmate...
My mouth opened in surprise, my face turning bright red.
(This is a mission... for the retreat... to protect Fuuma, that's why...)
I slipped my arm around his waist, pulling his body close and fixing us together.
We were close enough to feel each other's heat, breath, even the thump of each other's hearts.
...ah... ugh... w-what are you doing... are you trembling... this isn’t the time, we’re in the middle of a fight...
I tried to stay calm, but his strong body and warm heat wrapped around me, making my face feel like it might catch fire.
He really is an impressive commander... even aside from his combat skill, I can respect him... but—
As far as I can remember, I’ve never felt this way about him before.
Yet just looking up at him from this distance, seeing his serious profile, my face heated up, my breathing quickened, my heart raced.
If I don’t control my expression and he sees this face, I won’t be able to make any excuse—.
While I was thinking that and desperately willing myself to settle, Fuuma suddenly shouted and loosened her footing.
It’s fine, just stay like this.
Her words let Mai calm down in return.
The scent of approaching enemies, the battlefield air—it’s a mental stabilizer for a Taimanin.
Nodding at Mai’s words, Fuuma pressed her legs and sprinted through.
Huh, you’re wounded—still try to attack!
As the enemies, perhaps expecting us to stop, hesitated and shouted in confusion, they still followed the signal and launched a coordinated assault.
Anticipating the enemies’ moves—more like preparing for any possible action, Mai was already ready.
She scattered the paper she’d collected from all over her body, shaping each piece differently.
Like automatically folding origami, the transformed paper fluttered around, attacking the foes and preventing them from reaching us.
Yes! Ah, Fuuma—on the other side too!
Following Mai's command, Fuuma turned her stance toward that side, and Mai scattered paper in that direction as well.
Again and again, Fuuma moved on Mai's precise orders, while Mai kept the enemies stalled.
(…It somehow feels so easy to fight… Is it because Fuuma's with me…?)
Even though I doubted it, the two of them moved like seasoned Taimanin, perfectly in sync partners.
I got carried away by that thought and unintentionally let the paper defense lapse for a moment—.
The defeated enemy mustered its last strength, shattered the ground, and launched countless shards.
It was my mistake for neglecting the defense while gloating.
Hearing Fuuma's scream, Mai hurriedly pulled out more paper and used everything to erect a defensive wall.
The paper shield somehow blocked it, and just as Mai breathed a sigh of relief, a single pebble grazed her bangs.
Immediately after, a dull thud rang out and the impact surged through Fuuma's arm that was holding me.
I- I'm fine… phew… It just hit, it didn't pierce…
It was a lucky break—Fuuma's smiling face made an overwhelming guilt rise inside me.
Hey, hey, if Mai hadn't been here, I wouldn't know how many times I'd have been killed by now.
Tightening my slack arm and hugging Mai firmly again, Fuuma whispered in a slightly lower, serious voice.
More importantly, I'm glad you're safe, Mai.
Unintentionally, just hearing those words made my chest flutter and my face heat up.
It was the same feeling that had made my heartbeat race earlier.
With that thought, my heart fluttered and my mind swayed clearly, and then—.
A pebble, different from the one that brushed my bangs, had somehow torn my clothes.
Wait, please! No! Fuuma, you mustn't look!
Did you even look a little!?
While protesting, she hurriedly tried to hide her chest, reaching for his neck to pull his arm away—.
W-wait! No! If you let go at this speed, you'll fall!
Half panicking, Mai clung to him desperately, wrapping her arms around him and pressing her chest hard against him.
Just... just do it! This is the only way, shut up!
I held her to hide her chest, but the swell pressed hot against my body heat, thudding wildly.
(Ahhh... I was seen, seen... a man saw my... my breasts... I've been caught... sob)
It was beyond my control, but showing my breasts to someone I'm not even dating—how shameless.
(At this rate, I can never... get married... No, that's not... it's my fault for showing the captain...)
Clinging tightly, my mind was a whirlwind of fantasies, my face turning red then blue, a mess.
Above the frantic Mai, Fuuma's weak voice called out.
...Um, Mai? If possible, could you move a bit farther...
Wha—what are you saying! Do you want to see more!? I missed the chance, Captain...
No, that's not it! Look! It's hitting, it's hitting!
What do you mean it's hitting...
While they kept arguing, the two sprinted through the forest at full speed.
